title: Thermomix Pork Gyoza
description: Pork and wombok filling made in the Thermomix, bought wrappers, pan-fried for a crisp base then steamed lid-on.

steps.text: Salt the shredded cabbage ({{cabbage}}), rest 10 minutes, then squeeze it dry in the nut milk bag. Wet cabbage is the main cause of soggy filling.

Chop the spring onion ({{spring-onion}}), garlic ({{garlic}} cloves) and ginger in the bowl, then add the mince ({{mince}}), squeezed cabbage and seasonings. Mix 20 sec / Reverse / Speed 3 so it stays textured rather than pasted.
Chill the filling 20 minutes. Bought mince is looser than freshly minced shoulder, so do not skip this.
Wrap: a teaspoon of filling per wrapper ({{wrappers}}), wet the rim, pleat and press to seal.
Heat the cast iron properly before the oil goes in, then fry the bases until golden, in batches so they are not crowded.
Add a splash of water, cover, and steam 5–6 minutes.
Uncover and let the base re-crisp before lifting them out.

notes.title: Seasoning amounts still open
notes.text: The soy, sesame oil, mirin, sugar and white pepper quantities were never captured. Ask me to set them properly before the next batch.

notes.title: No lid for the cast iron
notes.text: A baking tray, a dinner plate or foil over the top all work for the steam step.

notes.title: Wrappers
notes.text: Round gyoza wrappers rather than square wonton skins. Most are sold frozen and want an hour in the fridge to thaw, otherwise they tear.

notes.title: Freezing
notes.text: Freeze them shaped, flat on a tray, then bag them. Cook from frozen adding about 2 minutes to the steam step. Do not freeze the loose raw filling.

notes.title: Air fryer
notes.text: 190°C for 8–10 minutes with a light oil spray. All-over crunch rather than a crisp base.
